chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna, from Sudayr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Among the happiness of a man is that he has a child in whom his resemblance is recognised — his physical form, his character, and his noble qualities.

key_terms.خُلُق: Character, moral disposition, manners — what a person is on the inside
key_terms.سَعَادَة: Felicity or happiness, used in the sense of divinely-given well-being, distinguished from mere worldly pleasure
key_terms.شَمَائِل: Noble qualities, virtues, characteristic traits (plural of shamila)
key_terms.شِبْه: Resemblance, likeness — the quality of looking or being like someone

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about the happiness of a man who has a child resembling him?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) identifies one of the sources of a man's felicity as having a child who resembles him in three distinct dimensions: physical appearance (khalq), moral character (khuluq), and virtuous qualities (shama'il). The hadith uses the word 'sa'ada' (felicity/happiness), a term with deep spiritual resonance in Islamic thought, indicating that such resemblance is not merely a biological pleasure but a form of God-given blessing. This teaching is situated within al-Kafi's chapter on child resemblance, addressing the natural human desire for continuity of one's qualities through one's offspring.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Musny, from Sudeyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘From happiness of the man is that there happens to be for him the son in whom his resemblance would be recognised, in his appearance, and his mannerisms, and his virtues’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Muthanna’ from Sadir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is of good fortune of a man to have a son who resembles his father, physically, morally and in his nature.”’
